draft.title: Reading graphs of real data
card: A graph of real data shows how one quantity changes with another, such as water depth against time. You can describe it even without a rule.
Read the graph from left to right. If the line goes up, the quantity is increasing. If it goes down, the quantity is decreasing.
A flat section means the quantity is not changing for those inputs. The graph is steady there, and the output stays at the same value.
Where the graph meets the vertical axis, the input is 0. Where it meets the horizontal axis, the output is 0.
draft.remember: Read left to right: up is increasing, down is decreasing, flat is no change, and an axis crossing means a zero.

a.q: A graph shows the depth of water in a tank (in cm) against time (in minutes). It is flat from 5 to 9 minutes. What happens to the depth then?
a.why: A flat section means the output does not change for those inputs, so the depth stays the same. It is not zero, because a flat line can sit at any height. It only reaches zero where it meets the horizontal axis.
a.clue: A flat line has the same height all the way along.

b.q: A graph shows the height of a drone (in m) above the ground against time (in s). It starts at the vertical axis at 20, falls, and meets the horizontal axis at 8. What does the point at 8 on the horizontal axis mean?
opts: The drone starts 8 metres above the ground
The drone is 8 metres up after 20 seconds
b.why: On the horizontal axis the output, the height, is 0, so the drone is on the ground. The input there is 8, so this happens at 8 seconds. The 20 is the starting height, where the graph meets the vertical axis.
b.clue: On the horizontal axis, which quantity is 0?
